_about: PHALANX rule registry (protocol v0.3 s1.2). Protocol names rules/rule_registry.yaml; kept here as JSON in docs/ because data/rules/ is frozen and the engine reads JSON only (no pyyaml). Machine-checked by phalanx.registry.check().

prefixes.MAP-CHK: mapping compatibility checks and decision composition

rules.title: Pass-1 derivation of S, TB and L from affected assets A (unnumbered in v1)
rules.description: Derives segments (Ground/Space/User/Human Resources) from the 'Segment:' prefixes of A, trust boundaries from segment pairs plus a Ground<->Core (NG) boundary from asset keywords or 'Ground: all assets', and lifecycle phases from per-segment spans and asset keywords; validates S against the stored value. v1 gives this block no rule number; LEG-R00 is a registry-assigned id (it was filed under LEG-R11 until 2026-10-18, when R11 was found defined as a separate boundary rule in the August 2026 mapping review).

rules.title: One threat -> many techniques
rules.description: Flag added for adversarial/enabling records (R1/R5): 1<->many ENISA threat to SPARTA techniques. A flag only; v1 computes no mapping.

rules.title: Confidence tagging
rules.description: Flag added to every record: each mapping carries a confidence grade (High/Med/Low). v1 only reports Conf as the analyst-entered value or PENDING.

rules.title: Countermeasure linkage
rules.description: Flag added for adversarial/enabling records: countermeasures attach to specific assets and interfaces, not whole categories. v1 emits CM=PENDING and computes no linkage.

rules.title: Multi-segment footprint -> bridging sub-chain
rules.description: Derived segment set S has >=2 members: flag; report asks for a bridging sub-chain IA->EX/LM->IMP across the segments. v1 does not emit the sub-chain. Revised in the August 2026 mapping review (slide 10): valid only when exactly one interface joins the two segments; outside that condition no boundary is assigned (removed false positives TR01, TR14, TR26). The frozen v1 code implements the unrevised form.

rules.title: Multi-lifecycle footprint
rules.description: Derived lifecycle set L has >=2 phases: flag; 'split only if TTP/CM differ'.

rules.title: Interface boundary where the operator or security domain changes
rules.description: Condition: an asset pair is joined by an interface and the operator or the security domain changes across it. Action: assign one interface boundary; endpoint location is recorded as an attribute, not a separate boundary. Layer: computed. Defined in the August 2026 mapping-rule review; not implemented in the frozen v1 code.

source.locator: slide 10 (rule table; build_mapping_review.py l.196-212); slide 11 evidence grades E1-E4

rules.title: Artifact admission boundary (design / manufacturing / transport / update)
rules.description: Condition: an artifact enters through the design, manufacturing, transport or update path and its effect is realised in operation. Action: the analyst assigns the boundary; confidence from evidence grades E1 (ENISA name/description names supply chain, third party, transport or update) - E2 (a SPARTA supply-chain technique realises it) - E3 (pre-operational asset with effect on operational assets) - E4 (analyst inference only, flagged for review). Negative rule: hazards acting on pre-operational assets are not admissions. Layer: judged. Defined in the August 2026 review; not implemented in v1 code.

source.locator: slide 10 (rule table; build_mapping_review.py l.196-212); slide 11 evidence grades E1-E4

rules.title: Authority exercised over equipment
rules.description: Condition: a party exercises authority over equipment. Action: computed when HR and technical assets are both present; judged when only descriptive evidence exists. Layer: mixed. Defined in the August 2026 review; not implemented in v1 code.

source.locator: slide 10 (rule table; build_mapping_review.py l.196-212); slide 11 evidence grades E1-E4

rules.title: Candidate lifecycle of the ETP
rules.description: Candidate lifecycle phases of a threat projection are copied from the legacy tuple L field (ENISA Annex C has no lifecycle column); the SI realized_lifecycle must lie inside. Replaces the v1 derivation from A for TR52.

rules.title: ETP selector scope definition
rules.description: Each ENISA Annex C affected-asset selector clause maps symbolically to documented segment/asset-class scope components (`assumed` where ENISA is silent). Registered from the SelectorPolicy slice's report.

rules.title: SI action window
rules.description: The SI covers initial access through effect; Reconnaissance and Resource Development are preparatory and outside the window (kind 'prep' fails the behavior check).

rules.title: Attacker-scoped graph instantiation
rules.description: Nodes/edges with scope 'attacker' exist in the instantiated graph only when the SI's attacker originates there.

rules.title: SI+G selector resolution
rules.description: Resolves each selector only against the selected SI's variant graph G, within ET-P-SEL-01 scope, yielding symbolic|scoped_resolved|partially_resolved|unresolved with evidence (invariant I8 bounds the scope). Registered from the SelectorPolicy slice's report.

rules.title: Candidate generator: T1 crosswalk
rules.description: ENISA threat -> workbook threat-based controls -> SafeMode enisa_control edges -> SPARTA technique.

rules.title: Candidate generator: attacker-class seeds
rules.description: Techniques whose access position matches the SI attacker class but that T1 does not reach. Additionally, the compromised authorized GS class is seeded with its entry steps IA-0007 and IA-0007.02, so on-board steps no longer depend on a threat's crosswalk for their entry.

rules.title: Candidate generator: legacy chain (regression)
rules.description: Techniques in the superseded Phalanx TR52 mapping; regression only.

rules.title: Candidate generator: deprecation successors
rules.description: Non-deprecated v4.0.1 Impact techniques IMP-0007..IMP-0014 (all v3.x IMP-0001..0006 are deprecated; T1 reaches no successor).

rules.title: Candidate generator: SPARTA SV-* claims
rules.description: Techniques SPARTA v4.0.1 relates to an SV-* threat statement claimed by the ET (threat `claims`); deprecated techniques dropped; Impact bridge to MAP-CG-04 successors. The same links supply the evidence check (MAP-CHK-09) when no authored clause covers the technique.

rules.title: Check: technique valid in the pinned SPARTA version
rules.description: Fails when the catalog marks the technique [DEPRECATED].

rules.title: Check: behavior inside the SI action window
rules.description: Fails for preparatory (kind prep) tactics (rule SI-I-WIN-01); prep techniques return after this check.

rules.title: Check: attacker class holds the required access position
rules.description: For entry/ground techniques the attacker class must be in profile.access; on-board techniques are not_applicable here and checked via reachability.

rules.title: Check: authority precondition
rules.description: B3: reads protection_applied.<edge>.<flag> on the command_authority edge from the attacker origin to a target asset (protected -> fail, unprotected -> pass, missing -> unknown; no edge -> fail). B2: reads every protection entry. Credential rule compares the SI credential.

rules.title: Check: technique target intersects SI selected assets
rules.description: Passes when profile.target meets SI.selected_asset_instances.

rules.title: Check: technique effect intersects SI intended effect
rules.description: Enabling techniques are not_applicable; others need an effect in the SI intended_effect (CIA set).

rules.title: Check: SI realized lifecycle in technique phases
rules.description: Passes when SI.realized_lifecycle is in profile.lifecycle.

rules.title: Check: path and on-board foothold
rules.description: B3 only (B2 not_applicable). Entry: a role edge from the attacker origin to a target asset; ground: attacker resides on a mission ground node; on-board: foothold from pass 1 (accepted entry -> pass; only unresolved entries -> unknown; none -> fail); plus requires_fact SI paths (missing -> unknown). Worst result wins.

rules.title: Check: ET-linked evidence clause supports the technique
rules.description: not_applicable when another check already failed; pass with the clause text when the technique is in an ET evidence clause; otherwise unknown. Clause rows are data rows of rules/evidence/<ET>.json. Additionally, also pass with the claimed SV id and its quote when the technique is related to a claimed SV-* statement; an authored clause takes precedence.

rules.title: Technique profile resolution
rules.description: Profile = tactic default, then exact-id override; parents never leak into sub-techniques.

rules.title: Decision composition
rules.description: Any fail -> rejected (reason codes = failing checks); else any unknown -> unresolved (reason codes = unknown checks); else accepted. Codes keep check order.

rules.title: Assurance-finding derivation
rules.description: AF types: insufficient_evidence, missing_system_state (unresolved MRs), candidate_inclusion_gap (a generator of kind attacker_seed/deprecation_successor without a baseline generator), unreachable (nothing accepted), no_framework_coverage (zero candidates; no MR, I11).

rules.title: Boundary-edge verdict candidates (applicable/adjacent/not_applicable)
rules.description: Per boundary-role edge: applicable = selected asset terminates it, edge active in the realized lifecycle, role named by the ETP; adjacent = same but role not named; else not_applicable. Candidate/adjacency classification only; 'crossed' belongs to BX-CHK-01. Full boundary candidate generation is Phase 3.

rules.title: Crossing validation
rules.description: 'crossed' is recorded only on an edge that an accepted entry action traverses (I4); precedence crossed > applicable > adjacent > not_applicable.

rules.title: AFG: on-board actions are preceded by an accepted entry
rules.description: pass if every accepted on-board action has an accepted traversing entry; not_applicable without a graph (B2).

rules.title: AFG: an accepted Impact step realises the intended effect
rules.description: pass when an accepted Impact action's effect meets SI.intended_effect; not_applicable with no accepted chain.

rules.title: AFG: ordering of accepted actions
rules.description: Accepted actions ordered ground, entry, then others; within a group by tactic order then id; consecutive actions form the edges. Construction rule, no verdict.

rules.title: Control-placement listing (no placement check yet)
rules.description: Lists SPARTA countermeasures of accepted techniques and the ENISA Annex D controls of the T1 crosswalk with placement 'not_adjudicated'. No placement check exists; Phase 3.

crosswalk.delta: v1 branched on the ENISA category (R1 adversarial, R5 enabling) and only flagged 'TTP expected'; it never computed techniques. The engine has no category gate: candidate generation runs for whichever ET is requested (pilot: TR52, category NAA) and every candidate is decided by MAP-CHK. R5's 'spawns an adversarial chain' is not modelled; enabling is a technique-profile effect value, not an ET category.

No current rule gates on failure categories (FM, UD); the pilot has no non-adversarial ET. Before the engine runs such an ET a rule must decide between no candidates (I11 no_framework_coverage) and not_applicable cells (protocol s1.1/s6.1).
State/outage-as-precondition is not modelled; no current rule consumes an ET category. Same open decision as LEG-R02.
Environmental category gate not modelled. Same open decision as LEG-R02.

v1 asserted a one-to-many cardinality flag. Now four generators propose candidates with recorded provenance (MR.generators) and each candidate gets its own decision; many-to-many is a computed result, not an assertion.
No High/Med/Low confidence grade exists. Replaced by status accepted|rejected|unresolved with system-state reason codes and root facts (MAP-CHK-11); the two are not convertible.
Legacy intent: countermeasures attach to specific assets and interfaces. Current CP-CHK-01 only lists countermeasures with placement 'not_adjudicated'; the attachment semantics return in Phase 3.

v1 flagged records spanning >=2 segments and asked for a bridging IA->EX/LM->IMP sub-chain. Now boundaries come from graph edges (BC-GEN-01) and the chain is built from accepted actions in order (AFG-CHK-03; AFG-CHK-01 requires entry before on-board action). The segment-count trigger is gone.

v1 flagged multi-phase lifecycle and deferred any split. Now the ETP states candidate phases (ET-P-LC-01) and each SI fixes one realized phase that is checked against the technique phases (MAP-CHK-07); a multi-phase ET becomes several SIs rather than a flag.

The Pass-1 block is split by output. Lifecycle (L): derived from A by keyword in v1, copied from the legacy tuple field in ET-P-LC-01 (provenance recorded; not equivalent in method, identical value for TR52). Trust boundaries (TB): v1 output as asserted boundaries is reclassified per plan v5 s10 as candidate/adjacency (BC-GEN-01) over graph edges; the Ground<->Core keyword heuristic is replaced by the architecture graph and security-domain membership. Segments (S): derivation from 'Segment:' prefixes is dropped (nodes carry segment/domain in G); selector scope is handled by ET-P-SEL-01 and SI-I-SEL-01.
No v1 counterpart: scenario action window, attacker-scoped instantiation, selector scope and resolution.
No v1 counterpart: attacker-seed, legacy-regression and deprecation-successor generators (v1 had no candidate generation).

No v1 counterpart: v1 left TTP, CM and Conf blank for the analyst. The nine compatibility dimensions (version, behavior, access_position, authority, target, effect, lifecycle, reachability, evidence), profile resolution and finding derivation are new (MAP-CHK-07 appears under LEG-R10).
No v1 counterpart: crossing validation (I4), attack-flow consistency checks, and control listing.

R11 assigned a boundary whenever operator or security domain changes across an interface. v2 records the change as data (node security_domain, edge crosses_security_domain, validated against endpoint domains) and does not derive a boundary from it: every edge carries a role, BC-GEN-01 gives the per-SI verdict (applicable/adjacent/not_applicable) from the threat's roles and the selected assets, and BX-CHK-01 allows 'crossed' only when an accepted action traverses the edge. A domain change alone neither creates nor crosses a boundary.

Not carried over as a rule. v2 models artifact admission structurally (boundary role artifact_admission on integration/update edges, verdicts via BC-GEN-01); the analyst assignment and the E1-E4 evidence grading have no v2 counterpart.

R13 decided whether a party has authority over equipment, computed from HR + technical assets or judged from text. v2 checks authority per technique from the SI's attacker credential and the protection state on the attacker's command_authority edge (MAP-CHK-04), with the attacker's origin and reachable nodes from SI-I-INST-01. HR assets are not modelled; there is no judged path.
